diffToSpecMapping.all_changes_traced: Every change in the diff traces to a spec requirement. No unexplained additions, deletions, or modifications found. The 7 changed files match the spec's file summary (3 new + 4 modified). The useAiJobApplicationSummary.ts hook has an added `enabled` guard which traces to the lazy-fetch requirement in the spec (section 'AI summary data fetching').

summary: All 5 QA Run 1 findings have been correctly fixed. No new HIGH findings identified. The implementation faithfully covers all spec requirements across all 8 files. The conditional route pattern ({isAiEnabled && <Route>}) is an accepted deviation per plan review. The hook enabled guard is an accepted minimal change per instructions. One borderline observation: the useAiJobApplicationSummary hook fires for any status where aiSummary.id exists (not just succeeded), making an unnecessary API call for pending/failed/etc. statuses. The spec says 'only when a summary exists and status is succeeded'. However, the enabled guard does prevent the critical failure case (fetching with id 0), and the extra call for non-succeeded statuses is wasteful but not harmful -- the data is gated by `status === 'succeeded'` before consumption (PlatoTab line 43). This does not rise to HIGH severity as it has zero user-visible impact and no correctness issue.
